metadata.title: Merchant Commerce Platform Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: How a merchant commerce platform must change when buying moves into AI assistants, payment partners or licensing change, low-value import exemptions disappear, or third-party data access is restricted.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: One hosted storefront per merchant renders the catalog, sends carts to a single checkout tied to one payment processor, and writes orders that apps read through broad API scopes.
metadata.residualArchitecture: The merchant's catalog, checkout rules, buyer identity and order record are surface-independent contracts. Any storefront, agent or channel uses the same checkout and identity; payment routes, duties and data-sharing policies are effective-dated configuration behind those contracts; apps act through narrow, auditable scopes and extensions.
metadata.note: Stressors are business-context changes, not outage drills, and carry no likelihood.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: AI assistants become the place where shoppers start and finish purchases
stressors.detection: Rising share of sessions and orders referred by AI surfaces; falling direct storefront traffic; agent checkout volume.
stressors.attractor: Demand concentrates in a few assistants that rank products from structured data and complete checkout without a storefront visit.
stressors.businessReaction: Make catalog data agent-ready, enable checkout inside assistants with the merchant's rules, and give merchants control and reporting per AI channel.
stressors.residue: Checkout and buyer identity are protocol endpoints usable by any surface; the storefront becomes one client among many.

impacts.effect: Reach means presence in assistants as well as storefront performance.
New channels include AI assistants with direct checkout.
The step becomes the primary acquisition path for some categories.
AI channel GMV share becomes a headline KPI.
Agentic channels become a core product rather than an add-on.
Owns catalog syndication and protocol checkout.
Must serve agents with the same rules as storefronts.
Becomes a primary demand stream.
Assistants may favor marketplaces unless merchant catalogs are equally structured.

stressors.name: A primary payment processing partner relationship changes or a market requires local licensing
stressors.detection: Partner contract notices, regulator guidance, licensing requirements in new markets, settlement exceptions.
stressors.attractor: Payment acceptance and payouts in a market depend on a different partner or a local licensed entity.
stressors.businessReaction: Route new payments through eligible partners, migrate tokens and payout instructions, and keep merchant balances whole.
stressors.residue: Payment routes and processors are configuration behind the payments API; the merchant ledger stays the source of truth independent of processor references.

impacts.effect: Getting paid reliably must survive partner changes.
Payments activation depends on the market's licensed route.
Penetration can drop where integrated payments are unavailable.
Must present stable behavior while routes change.
Routes by market capability rather than a fixed processor.
Preserves balances independently of the processor.
Payout continuity must hold across partner migrations.

stressors.name: A major import market removes its duty exemption for low-value parcels
stressors.detection: Customs rule changes, carrier notices, spikes in refused parcels and duty-related returns.
stressors.attractor: Cross-border orders that were duty-free now incur duties and customs data requirements, raising landed cost and delivery failures.
stressors.businessReaction: Collect duties at checkout, require tariff codes on products, and adjust market pricing and carrier choices.
stressors.residue: Duties, customs data and market pricing are effective-dated rules resolved at checkout per destination.

impacts.effect: Launching a market includes duty and customs readiness.
Duties-included share becomes critical to conversion.
Calculates duties with up-to-date rules.
Adjusts market pricing for landed cost.
Generates customs data with labels.
Market launch flow includes customs data quality.

stressors.name: Regulators restrict sharing shopper data with third-party apps
stressors.detection: New privacy rules or enforcement on data processors, app data incidents, merchant compliance requests.
stressors.attractor: Apps can no longer receive broad customer data; merchants remain liable for processors they install.
stressors.businessReaction: Narrow scopes, require protected-data approval, move app logic into sandboxed extensions and functions, and audit access.
stressors.residue: Partner capabilities run as extensions and functions close to the data with minimal, audited scopes.

impacts.effect: Partner growth depends on building inside platform boundaries.
Apps rely on extensions rather than data export.
Protected-data compliance becomes a listing requirement.
Developer platform prioritizes extension surfaces.
Enforces narrow scopes and protected-data approval.
Hosts partner logic in sandboxes.
Review includes data-minimization checks.
